text:
The Blackhawks learned this weekend that their captain is gone for a long while. Connor Bedard will have surgery to repair his right shoulder this week, The Athletic's Scott Powers and Mark Lazerus reported, and ESPN's estimated return is March 1. He had 18 points in 15 games. Chicago has played two without him, and the minutes have flowed to Frank Nazar, up to 22:30 a night from 17:51, with Ryan Donato taking Bedard's spot beside Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi.

The kids have answered so far. Sam Rinzel won it in overtime in Calgary last night and has 15 points in ten games, twelve of them in the last five; he has been on the top power play since Bowen Byram went on injured reserve. Nazar has a five-game point streak (six goals, one assist), and Patrick Kane ended the longest goal drought of his career, 18 games, and had three points last night. We don't have a confirmed Chicago starter yet, so the goaltending question stays open into the evening.

Vancouver is in its own holding pattern. Elias Pettersson (upper body) is out while his name fills the trade columns, and Marco Rossi took over: two goals against his former team, Minnesota, in a shootout win last night, including the late tying goal, set up by Brock Boeser, who has points in ten straight. Nikita Tolopilo starts over Leevi Meriläinen, who has 17 of the Canucks' 25 starts; Tolopilo stopped .944 in his only game, a one-game sample that tells you little.

Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back, and both live in their own end: Chicago has 43% of the five-on-five expected goals, Vancouver 40%, and the Canucks allow the most expected goals per 60 in the league. That's why two Blackhawks made our Sleepers: Donato at 17% to score, and Nazar at 62% for a point, well above his season pace of 48%. Our numbers have it nearly even, 3.20 expected goals for Chicago, 3.17 for Vancouver.
headline: Blackhawks, without Bedard, meet Canucks without Pettersson
